data.name: Evil Orbs
data.detailed_description:
We think they came from space. We think they are evil. But, we know they have invaded the cities of Earth and made all life a bummer, so they must be destroyed. However, they are impervious to all forms of conventional weaponry.





Fortunately for humanity, Dr. Klaus von Hammersphere has discovered the rare element AntiOrbium which sends the Evil Orbs back to whence they came (wherever that is) and he has invented a device that he affectionately calls the “Elementary Evil Orb Disposal Device 2000” (EEODD 2000 for short) which can be used to shoot and deflect balls of AntiOrbium at the Orbs. He is recruiting you to wield this device and save humanity. What do you say? Do you want to save humanity?



CONTROLS

Use your mouse to control the EEODD 2000 and fire balls of AntiOrbium at the Evil Orbs. Because AntiOrbium is a very rare element, there is only so much to go around. Fortunately, you can also use the EEODD to control the balls after you have fired them at the orbs and try to knock the balls back at remaining Orbs to maximize the amount of Orbs popped per each AntiOrbium ball fired.



GAME

The Evil Orbs are devious and have utilized common materials from Earth to protect themselves from your barrage of AntiOrbium.




As in any armed conflict between humans and mysterious Orb-like entities, Dr. Hammersphere is hard at work inventing special powerups for your EEODD 2000 to win the arms race with the Evil Orbs. Utilize these powerups in different combinations to overcome whatever the Evil Orbs throw at you.





Once you have popped all the Evil Orbs in a city, the cloud of total bummerness will dissipate from the newly saved city, and the residents will celebrate your victory with a party. But, no time for you to stand around celebrating, for you must save all 132 cities around the world in order to stop the Evil Orbs before they complete their plan for world domination.

Save a city by using fewer AntiOrbium balls, and Dr. Hammersphere will reward you with a medal for your thriftiness. Can you earn gold medals on every level?



Along the way, you and Dr. Hammersphere just might solve the mystery of where the Evil Orbs came from in the first place.

Can you beat the Challenge Mode?

Challenge your friends and duel them either over the network or hotseat!

Save replays of your awesome shots and amaze your friends and family! Post them online and become the gaming star that you have always imagined yourself to be!

Can you earn all 120 trophies?

reviews.review:
Evil Orbs takes the familiar satisfaction of bouncing projectiles around an enclosed playfield and turns it into a cheerful action-puzzle game about saving the planet from a strangely shaped invasion. Developed and published by GoBit Games, it presents a deliberately silly scenario in which mysterious spherical creatures have occupied cities around the world and proven resistant to conventional weapons. Humanity's answer is AntiOrbium, a rare substance discovered by the eccentric Dr. Klaus von Hammersphere, who equips the player with the Elementary Evil Orb Disposal Device 2000. The story is mostly an excuse for the gameplay, but its playful attitude gives the campaign plenty of personality.

The main attraction is the unusual mixture of aiming, ricocheting, and resource management. Players use the mouse to launch AntiOrbium balls toward the invading orbs, but ammunition is limited because the substance is supposedly extremely rare. Instead of treating every projectile as disposable, the game encourages you to keep a ball active and redirect it toward additional targets. A successful attempt can therefore become a satisfying sequence of rebounds in which one shot destroys several enemies. This makes careful positioning and anticipation considerably more important than simply firing as quickly as possible.

Levels become increasingly puzzle-oriented because the invaders protect themselves with ordinary materials found on Earth. Obstacles interfere with straightforward shots and encourage experimentation with angles and rebounds. Power-ups for the EEODD 2000 expand the possibilities further, and learning how to combine these abilities with the basic mechanics gives later encounters more variety. The controls are easy to understand, but earning an efficient result requires better timing and planning than the game's colorful appearance initially suggests.

The campaign offers a substantial 132 cities to rescue. Clearing every orb removes the gloomy cloud hanging over a city, but merely completing a stage is not necessarily the end of it. Finishing levels while consuming fewer AntiOrbium balls earns medals, including gold medals for particularly efficient performances. This scoring structure gives completionists a meaningful reason to replay stages. A solution that initially seems acceptable can often be refined by finding a better angle or keeping a projectile in circulation longer.

There is also more secondary content than might be expected from such a compact arcade game. Challenge Mode provides another test after players become comfortable with the standard mechanics, while 120 in-game trophies create a long list of optional accomplishments. Steam achievements, leaderboards, cloud support, and replay saving complement the progression systems. Being able to preserve an especially elaborate shot is a fitting addition because some of the most enjoyable moments come from watching a projectile unexpectedly continue bouncing through several targets.

Multiplayer broadens the package further. Competitive matches can be played over a network or through local hotseat-style play, and the Steam version supports online PvP, shared or split-screen functionality, cross-platform multiplayer, and Remote Play Together. The competitive side is not necessarily the primary reason to play, but it prevents the experience from being entirely dependent on the campaign. Trying to outperform another player can make the simple projectile mechanics surprisingly entertaining.

The presentation is intentionally modest and colorful rather than technically elaborate. Its cartoonish approach fits the absurd story and makes the game feel approachable, while the humorous names and exaggerated premise prevent it from becoming overly serious. Hardware requirements are extremely light, so performance should not be demanding on ordinary PCs. The downside is that players expecting modern visual spectacle or extensive narrative development will not find either here. The fundamental gameplay loop can also become repetitive during longer sessions, especially for anyone who is not interested in improving medals or pursuing optional objectives.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently unverified, with no official Steam Deck compatibility rating displayed for the game. Its Steam listing officially specifies Windows and macOS support rather than SteamOS/Linux, and its gameplay was originally designed around mouse control. It may potentially be possible to experiment with Proton and custom trackpad or controller mappings, but this should not be interpreted as guaranteed compatibility. Players specifically purchasing it for Steam Deck should therefore consider its handheld support unknown rather than officially supported.

Evil Orbs works best as a casual arcade puzzler that gradually rewards precision. Its premise is amusing, its mechanics are immediately understandable, and the scarcity of ammunition gives every shot more importance than a traditional brick-breaking design. The 132-city campaign, medals, power-ups, Challenge Mode, trophies, multiplayer features, achievements, and replay system provide enough incentives to continue beyond simply finishing each stage once. Repetition eventually becomes noticeable, but players who enjoy optimizing trajectories and squeezing maximum value from a single projectile can find plenty of satisfaction here.

It is a charming and mechanically sound action-puzzle game that builds surprising depth from a straightforward bouncing-projectile concept. Its strongest qualities are efficient level design, satisfying ricochets, replayable medal challenges, and a healthy amount of additional content, making it an appealing choice for fans of casual games with a puzzle-solving edge.

Rating: 7/10
